Article Title: 'Cordial discussions': JP Nadda meets anti-reservation group after Jantar Mantar protest
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Union minister JP Nadda on Thursday met representatives of Reservation Hatao Andolan, which is protesting against caste-based reservation and demanding a complete overhaul at the national capital's Jantar Mantar.In a social media post on X, Nadda said that he met Harsh Dubey, Mrityunjay Pathak and Ran Bahadur Singh Chauhan as per the pre-determined schedule, adding that another meeting will be held soon."Following the movement that took place at Jantar Mantar on August 21, cordial discussions were held, as per the pre-determined schedule, with Shri Harsh Dubey, Shri Ran Bahadur Singh Chauhan, and Shri Mrityunjay Pathak, members of the team. In this connection, we will meet again soon," he said.However, Nadda did not give details of the meeting.Meanwhile, Harsh Dubey said that the meeting was an important step towards dialogue."Positive initiative for the welfare of all society today. Our team met with the honourable Shri JP Nadda Ji. During this time, there was a brief discussion with him regarding the demonstration that took place on August 21. This meeting is an important step towards dialogue.We will soon meet again with the honourable Nadda Ji and strive to move forward with a positive and just decision in the interest of all society," Dubey said."Our objective is not against any section, but rather to democratically and peacefully present our views for equal opportunities, a just system, and necessary reforms in the national interest. Further information and decisions regarding this will be officially communicated shortly," he added.Reservation Hatao Andolan is demanding that quotas in academics and employment should strictly be determined by income levels rather than social or caste identities. Additionally, the protesters advocated for a "one family, one reservation" policy and demanded the immediate withdrawal of the UGC's 2026 caste-equity directives.A large number of people gathered at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on Friday to protest against caste-based reservation, following which the Delhi Police and Central Forces were deployed at the protest site to maintain law and order.Security personnel were seen present at Jantar Mantar as protesters assembled at the designated protest area. The police deployment was carried out as a precautionary measure amid the large gathering.Reservation Hatao Andolan (RHA) is an official Instagram page with 5.6 million followers. The platform rapidly gained traction by adopting the protest-mobilisation tactics of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and has now called for a physical protest against the reservation system.
Article Summary: Union minister jp nadda met representatives of reservation hatao andolan. Protesters are protesting against caste-based reservation and demanding overhaul at jantar mantar. Harsh dubey, mrityunjay pathak and ran bahadur singh chauhan attended the meeting.

Article Title: Delhi HC quashes criminal defamation case against senior advocate Pinaki Misra
Article Text:
The Delhi High Court has quashed criminal defamation proceedings against senior advocate and former Member of Parliament Pinaki Misra

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: The Delhi High Court has quashed criminal defamation proceedings against senior advocate and former Member of Parliament Pinaki Misra, in a case alleging that he had said certain objectionable words about a lawyer in an interview.The high court also quashed a trial court's April 2019 order summoning Misra to face trial for defamation, saying permitting the proceedings to continue would not advance the cause of justice.Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma said the complainant had examined himself as the sole witness and had not provided any material to prima facie demonstrate that the alleged imputation had lowered his reputation in others' estimation."There is no material on record, in the form of statement of any other person or otherwise, to prima facie demonstrate that the alleged imputation had the effect of lowering the reputation of Respondent No 2 (complainant) in the estimation of others."The allegation that the publication caused damage to his reputation, by itself, remains an assertion of the complainant and does not establish the statutory requirement contemplated by Explanation 4 to Section 499 (defamation) of IPC," the court said in its order passed on August 25.The high court said permitting the criminal proceedings to continue would not advance the cause of justice and instead subject the petitioner (Misra) to the rigours of a criminal trial in the absence of sufficient foundational material."Accordingly, this court deems it appropriate, in exercise of its jurisdiction under Section 482 of CrPC, to quash the impugned summoning order and the consequential proceedings arising therefrom. The petition is accordingly allowed," it said.It was alleged that the complainant advocate had filed a complaint with the Bar Council of Delhi in 2018 against Misra, alleging that the senior advocate's appearance on behalf of power distribution companies before the National Green Tribunal amounted to professional misconduct.After the dispute was reported in a newspaper, it was alleged that Misra gave an interview to another newspaper in which he purportedly used certain objectionable words against the complainant.The complainant filed two defamation complaints alleging that Misra's objectionable remarks have lowered his reputation in the eyes of the public and also affected his professional life.The high court, in its order, noted that the allegation against Misra was founded upon the contents of an online news report.It said Misra had specifically denied having given the interview and had communicated in March 2019 to the editor of the news establishment, denying that he gave the alleged interview and seeking the publication's clarification.The court said the alleged imputation was founded upon an online news report, which has not been supported by examination of the concerned reporter, author, editor or any other person associated with the news portal, particularly when the petitioner had specifically denied having made the alleged statement and had also sent a communication seeking clarification in this regard.PTI
Article Summary: Delhi high court quashes criminal defamation proceedings against senior advocate and former member of parliament pinaki misra. The high court also quashed a trial court's april 2019 order summoning misra to face trial for defamation.

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, reiterating the Congress' demand to maintain the existing strength of the Lok Sabha at 543 for another 25 years.Kharge's letter came after Union parliamentary affairs minister hinted at a possible special session of Parliament for the passage of the Delimitation Bill.In his letter, Kharge urged the government to convene an all-party meeting to discuss its proposed delimitation exercise before any such session."I have written to PM Modi on delimitation, the delay in prorogation of the Monsoon Session of Parliament, and the likely special session mentioned by the Union minister of parliamentary affairs in a television interview last evening," Kharge said."I had last written to you on July 16, 2026 requesting you to convene an All-Party meeting for discussing the Government's proposals for delimitation. Article Title: Caste count method in Census ‘misleading’: Congress letter to PM
Article Text:
The letter from Kharge and Rahul said govt should prepare a fresh questionnaire through consultations with parties.

NEW DELHI: Terming the methodology for caste count adopted in Census 2027 “misleading” as it will not give a headcount of OBCs, leaders of opposition in Parliament, Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, have written to PM Narendra Modi demanding the Census questionnaire on caste notified recently be abandoned and a new one be drafted. They underlined that the word “OBC” has not even been used in the Census.In the backdrop of the controversy triggered by the questionnaire, Kharge and Rahul told the PM “your govt” has adopted an “open-ended question” to collect information about caste, and enumerators will have to take for an answer whatever a person replies to the caste question. They argued that a caste is known by different names and sub-castes depending on the region, which would result in one caste being recorded by thousands of names. “This would result in lakhs of castes being registered in the country, and the entire data recorded in the caste census would become useless,” the letter said.“We don’t approve of the caste census being done through this methodology. Govt should cancel the present questionnaire and prepare a fresh one through consultations with political parties, experts, and the public so that a correct headcount of every caste and community is collected and the caste census is precise, relevant, and beneficial,” it said.It said a readymade solution to the problem is that a “drop-down menu” comprising a list of castes be added to the questionnaire. “This very methodology is used for counting SCs and STs (in Census)... This methodology was adopted in the surveys of Bihar and Telangana. We are enclosing the caste lists of the two surveys for understanding.” Further, the letter said such a list of castes for Census can easily be compiled on the basis of the existing Socially and Educationally Backward Classes list and data from the Anthropological Survey of India.Releasing the letter, AICC spokesperson Jairam Ramesh and OBC department chairperson Anil Jaihind said govt had, in an affidavit to SC in Sept 2021, submitted that a “drop-down menu” with a list of castes will have to be used if a caste census were to be done. Ramesh said census enumerators can carry the said list of OBCs and record precise answers. He accused govt of “sabotaging” the caste census.
Article Summary: The letter from kharge and rahul said govt should prepare a fresh questionnaire through consultations with parties. They underlined that the word “obc’ has not even been used in the census. Aicc spokesperson jairam ramesh and obc department chairperson anil jaihind accused govt of ‘sabotaging’ the caste census.

NEW DELHI: A training aircraft belonging to Kanpur’s Garg Aviation crashed on Thursday, killing two — the trainer and trainee pilots — on board. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation said in a statement the Tecnam P2006T twin-engine aircraft (VT-NBV) crashed about five nautical miles from Kanpur Civil Airport, near Ganga Barrage.“The aircraft was on a training flight in the local flying area of Kanpur Civil Airport. There were two persons on board, a trainee pilot and an instructor. Both sustained fatal injuries in the accident. A team of three officials from the DGCA is proceeding to the site for necessary regulatory oversight and coordination,” said the DGCA statement.The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has been informed and “will undertake a detailed investigation into the accident in accordance with the applicable rules. The circumstances and cause of the accident will be determined through the investigation,” it added.Senior pilots call for a thorough investigation into the flying school operations.On June 26, 2026, a trainee pilot had got grievously injured while deboarding VT-NBV with the propeller running at Kanpur’s Chakeri Airport. Following this lapse, the DGCA had on June 28 said in a statement that it had “directed VT-NBV aircraft should not be utilised pending the probe.” Subsequently the aircraft started flying again till it crashed on Thursday.
Article Summary: The aircraft was on a training flight in the local flying area of kanpur civil airport. The aircraft accident investigation bureau (aaib) has been informed and “will undertake a detailed investigation into the accident in accordance with the applicable rules”

Article Title: Nepal flood: Centre puts Bihar & UP on high alert as NDRF deploys teams

NEW DELHI: In view of the flash flood situation in Nepal, Union home minister Amit Shah Wednesday spoke with CMs of Bihar and UP and assured all help to border districts, including deployment of additional National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams. The administrations of these districts have been put on high alert.“Govt of India stands with Nepal in this hour of crisis. I spoke with CMs of Bihar and UP regarding the disaster in Nepal. In border areas likely to be affected, local administration and rescue teams, along with NDRF, have been placed on high alert,” Shah said on X, expressing condolences to families of those who lost their loved ones in the disaster.Officers of home affairs, external affairs, jal shakti and defence ministries are monitoring the situation.Water level on Nepal-side reservoirs is reducing and the situation is under control. No panic-like situation has arisen, according to Central Water Commission (CWC).NDRF had earlier said the flash floods in the Nepal-China border region has led to a sudden rise in water level in Trishuli river at Furke Khola in Nepal, around 160 km from the Indian border, and the flood wave is likely to travel downstream in Gandak river.“Local authorities in Bihar and UP near the India-Nepal border along Gandak river have been advised to remain alert and maintain close monitoring of the situation,” NDRF said. In close coordination with the states and CWC, NDRF is keeping a close watch on the situation and has kept additional teams on standby for emergent requirements in case of any “unforeseen” situation.Out of nine NDRF teams deployed in Bihar, two have been dispatched for deployment in West Champaran and Muzaffarpur. The state govt is monitoring the situation and, in case of requirement, additional teams will be deployed.

Article Title: Flood-rescued elephant Joymoti airlifted and shifted to Anant Amabani’s Vantara for specialised care
Article Text:
Ensuring the highest standards of welfare during air transport

Joymoti’s story highlights the need for specialised veterinary care facilities closer to where wildlife emergencies occur

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Joymoti, a 53-year-old female elephant rescued from the devastating floods in Nagaland and Assam in July, was airlifted and moved to Vantara, Jamnagar, where she has already begun receiving immediate and specialised veterinary treatment.The elephant was swept away by floodwaters in Nagaland during the second week of July and was subsequently rescued by local communities with the assistance of government agencies. She sustained multiple injuries during the incident, including wounds to her forehead, right ear, the area above her tail, left inner thigh and abdomen, as well as a deep, maggot-infested wound around her external genital area. Her right eye is severely damaged, leaving her blind in that eye, with persistent tearing. She also has longstanding lameness in her left hind leg, resulting from a fracture sustained during logging, which affects her ability to walk normally and access food and water.Following her rescue, Joymoti received first aid and primary veterinary care locally, including wound dressing, pain medication, multivitamin and mineral supplements and supportive treatment. However, given the severity and multiple locations of her injuries, her advancing age and existing mobility challenges, she requires immediate treatment in a specialised hospital setting.Joymoti's transfer to Vantara is solely for immediate and specialised veterinary treatment. The decision to airlift her has been taken with her welfare and medical needs at the centre, allowing her to reach a specialised elephant hospital while minimising the duration and physical demands of ground transportation. Upon arrival at Vantara, Joymoti will undergo a comprehensive veterinary assessment and receive specialised treatment for her injuries and eye condition, along with nutritional and supportive care as required.Transporting an elephant by air for specialised hospital care is an unusual undertaking in India, requiring extensive veterinary, animal-care and logistical planning. Joymoti's transfer is being planned and carried out with careful attention to her health, comfort and safety at every stage, from her veterinary assessment and preparation before travel to loading, monitoring during the flight and her arrival at the hospital.Air transport can significantly reduce the duration of a long-distance journey for an animal requiring urgent medical attention. For elephants with serious injuries, chronic health conditions or mobility challenges, reducing journey time and avoiding prolonged ground travel can be an important consideration in protecting their welfare.Joymoti’s case also highlights the importance of having specialised elephant veterinary care facilities closer to areas where elephants are affected by floods, human-wildlife conflict and other health emergencies.Vantara has proposed the establishment of three wildlife veterinary care centres in Assam, including a dedicated centre for elephants, to strengthen local capacity for wildlife emergency veterinary care. The proposed centres would include species-specific facilities and veterinary support, enabling animals in need to receive timely and appropriate treatment closer to where emergencies occur. The centres would be operated completely independently by the Assam Forest Department.The aim is to strengthen local capacity so that elephants and other wildlife in Assam can receive high-quality care closer to home, avoiding the need for long-distance transportation whenever specialised treatment is required.Joymoti’s journey to Vantara is not a permanent relocation, but an urgent medical transfer undertaken solely to provide the specialised lifesaving treatment she currently requires. Her case underscores the importance of strengthening local veterinary capacity while ensuring that animals requiring advanced care can access it safely and without delay. At Vantara, the immediate priority is to provide Joymoti with the specialised treatment she needs and the best possible chance of recovery and a healthy, safe and dignified life.
Article Summary: Joymoti, a 53-year-old female elephant, was rescued from the devastating floods in nagaland and assam in july. She sustained multiple injuries, including wounds to her forehead, right ear, the area above her tail, left inner thigh and abdomen. Her right eye is severely damaged, leaving her blind in that eye, with persistent tearing.

NEW DELHI: Responding to letters written by SC judge Sandeep Mehta complaining against Rajasthan high court acting chief justice (ACJ) Sanjeev Prakash Sharma and seeking his transfer outside the state, CJI Surya Kant Wednesday said he has sought the ACJ’s response.Justice Mehta wrote three letters in as many weeks pleading for the transfer of Justice Sharma, who is retiring Sept 26, and appointment of a regular chief justice. Justice Mehta also complained as to why CJI Kant had not acted on his fervent pleas.Justice Mehta, who also hails from Rajasthan HC, has accused Justice Sharma of lacking in leadership qualities and alleged there was maladministration and malpractice on both judicial and administrative sides of HC.CJI Kant told TOI that the matter can be resolved only as per the established mechanism. “The Supreme Court cannot allow individual complaints concerning judges to be determined through competing claims in the media,” he said. He also released a public statement Wednesday decrying the attempt to hold a public trial over allegations made by one judge against another.Contents of the letters cannot be adjudicated in public domain and that judge concerned must be given a fair opportunity to place his response before any conclusion is reached.The fact that allegations have been made, therefore, cannot by itself be treated as a finding against the judge,” CJI Surya Kant’s statement said.The established mechanism for inquiring into allegations of an Supreme Court or High Court judge is the constitution of an in-house committee — comprising judges — by the Chief Justice of India, if he finds the response of the judge accused of misdemeanour or corrupt practices unsatisfactory and feels the charges are serious enough to warrant a deeper probe.CJI Kant, who is on a three-day official visit to Germany, also told TOI that he has already sought a response from Justice Sharma following the letters from Justice Mehta, who has alleged that there is “clear evidence of favouritism” by Justice Sharma. Justice Mehta’s complaints are being examined, CJI Surya Kant said.
Article Summary: Cji surya kant wednesday said he has sought the acj’s response. Justice mehta wrote three letters in as many weeks pleading for the transfer of justice sharma, who is retiring sept 26. Cji kant told toi that the matter can be resolved only as per the established mechanism.

Article Title: Dissidents push for Hindu Pradesh Congress Committee chief to end Punjab crisis
Article Text:
Dissident netas, including Charanjit Channi (L), have been seeking the replacement of Amarinder Raja Warring as the Punjab Cong chief

NEW DELHI: Congress is again mulling the idea of appointing a Hindu state president in Punjab amid a push from dissidents for a compromise to end the turmoil in the state unit.Well-placed sources said the deadlock in the dissidence-ridden organisation has cast a cloud over the upcoming election campaign, and the party brass is cut up about the unsuccessful fire-fighting efforts of key managers.A group of dissidents that includes senior netas like Charanjit Channi and Sukhjinder Randhawa has been seeking the replacement of state chief Amarinder Raja Warring ever since the AICC announced a clutch of poll-related panels while sticking with Warring at the helm two months ago.Now, sources said, the dissidents themselves have proposed that a Hindu Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) chief be appointed. This group has also conveyed that they will be on board with such a replacement, even though each one of them has been fancying their chances till now, they added.With the state chief and the leader of opposition both belonging to the Jatt Sikh community, the idea of a Hindu PCC chief is meant to bring balance to the organisational set-up.This was the original idea before the AICC decided to retain Warring at the top.An insider said the party is looking at its options and may have to make some change in the leadership position — either the Punjab chief or AICC in-charge, or both. While it is too close to the elections for such an organisational overhaul, the sources said the crisis has to be defused.Sources also dismissed the notion that Rahul Gandhi will soon kickstart the state campaign in the form of a bus journey, arguing that the bus would bring all the squabbling netas together and, thereby, enforce peace.A party manager said Rahul will only start the bus journey after the organisational bickering is over.“The campaign will be about the state and state Congress. It needs an agenda so that the party can set a narrative for voters,” he said. “The state netas will have to come together and draw up a plan for winning the election together. Only then will Rahul get into it,” the party functionary said.Also, Rahul will be a part of the bus campaign for 2-3 days, and state netas will steer the rest of it for around 20 days. While Congress was hopeful of its chances in the AAP-governed state, persistent infighting in the local unit has raised concerns about its prospects.Inputs that forces like jailed MP Amritpal Singh’s “Waaris Punjab De” may be gaining ground have further alarmed some strategists.

Article Title: 3 lakh tonnes of refined sugar to enter market
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: In what could improve availability of sugar in the market immediately and bring down prices, around 3-3.5 lakh tonnes available with Indian sugar refiners, who import raw sugar duty-free and export it after processing, is likely to come into the domestic market following a recent govt decision.Last week, govt had allowed duty-free import of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar and also allowed the processors to sell some refined sugar, which was meant for export only, in the domestic market. Officials and industry insiders said at least 3 lakh tonnes of processed sugar could come into the market quickly. The subsequent import of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar will help tide over any supply issue.Meanwhile, the ex-mill price of sugar has gone down by 20% in the past 10 days. Industry sources and officials said the ex-mill price in Kolhapur fell to Rs 48 per kg Wednesday and was around Rs 53 a kg in Uttar Pradesh.An official said ex-mill prices increasing from Rs 48 per kg to Rs 58-60 per kg in just a few days showed that speculation and stocking were the main reasons behind the price spike, and there had been no shortage.Deepak Ballani, director general of Indian Sugar Mills Association, the country’s top sugar industry body, said that govt measures to rationalise sugar prices had started showing results. “Over the last few days, ex-mill sugar prices have declined by nearly 20%, and we expect this reduction to be reflected in retail prices very soon. There is adequate availability of sugar in the country, and consumers will get the commodity at reasonable prices during the forthcoming festive season,” he added.On Wednesday, the average retail price of sugar was Rs 65 per kg.

Article Title: Low beam by default: Centre to tighten headlamp norms
Article Text:
CURBING THE GLARE: The steps target a major cause of crashes — high beams can briefly blind motorists coming from opposite direction

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From next April, automatic headlamps in new two-wheelers will work only in passing beam (low beam) mode, and headlamps of cars and other vehicles will have less intense illumination to reduce glare considering that such lights cause visual discomfort or impairs the vision of other road users.The road transport ministry has proposed these changes, along with the mandatory provision for buses and other heavy vehicles to use genuine reflective tapes to improve visibility at night and in bad weather, through draft amendments to Central Motor Vehicles Rules. The amendments in automotive vehicle standards are being made because efforts to persuade drivers and make them aware of the need to use low-beam mode have not yielded desired results.At present, the Automatic Headlamp On (AHO) system can switch on both low beam and high beam modes depending on vehicle settings. The proposed rule mandates that when the automatic system is active, the headlamp will be on low beam.As for high-intensity headlamps, the maximum permissible intensity has been reduced from 1.5 lakh candela or cd (official base unit of luminous intensity) to 1 lakh cd for two-wheelers.The maximum permissible intensity for four-wheelers (cars) has been reduced from 2.25 lakh cd to 1.5 lakh cd.Studies show that white light emitted from headlamps and front fog lamps with higher colour temperatures cause significant glare, leading to discomfort and reduced visibility for other road users. To address this issue, the maximum permissible colour temperature has been restricted to 6,500 Kelvin (K).It has also been proposed that the mounting height of main-beam headlamps be equivalent to that prescribed for passing-beam headlamps.These measures target one of the major causes of night-time road crashes in India — drivers using headlamps on high beam in urban areas, which can temporarily blind motorists approaching from the opposite direction, reducing visibility and increasing the risk of crashes.TOI has learnt the new-generation system will also include an audio alert to discourage unnecessary use of high-beam mode on city roads. If a driver manually switches to high beam in urban conditions, the vehicle will prompt them to shift back to low beam.However, the alert will be speed sensitive. Drivers travelling on highways at speeds above 60 kmph won’t receive the warning, since the use of high-beam mode may be necessary on poorly illuminated highway stretches. The feature is intended to promote safer driving behaviour in urban areas while ensuring that highway driving is not adversely affected, officials said.
Article Summary: From next april, automatic headlamps in new two-wheelers will work only in passing beam (low beam) mode. Headlamps of cars and other vehicles will have less intense illumination to reduce glare. Road transport ministry has proposed these changes, along with the mandatory provision for buses and other heavy vehicles to use genuine reflective tapes.

Article Title: Lok Sabha Secretariat issues notices to 20 rebel TMC MPs

NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha Secretariat has issued notices to 20 rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs who have aligned with NCPI and sought their responses within seven days on petitions filed by TMC national general secretary and MP Abhishek Banerjee seeking their disqualification under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution that lays down the anti-defection framework.Dated Aug 25, the notices to the 20 rebel MPs forward a copy of Banerjee’s petition dated June 18 filed against the MPs under Rule 6 of the Members of Lok Sabha (Disqualification on Ground of Defection) Rules, 1985.In a post on X, TMC Lok Sabha MP Mahua Moitra shared the photo of one of the notices issued to rebel MPs and said, “Cover up caught out!” Highlighting that TMC had filed 20 disqualification petitions in June, Moitra said, “Speaker LS did nothing except give them better seats at our expense. SG Tushar Mehta in Court said the Speaker had issued notices. Notice dated Aug 25th -- exact date of hearing!”On Tuesday, Supreme Court sought a response from Lok Sabha Speaker’s office on time-bound adjudication of TMC’s petition seeking disqualification of rebel MPs who broke away from the party after its electoral debacle in West Bengal, even as Abhishek Banerjee accused Speaker Om Birla of “deliberate inaction”.The SC also issued notices to the 20 rebel MPs: Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, Sudip Bandyopadhyay, Satabdi Roy, Prasun Banerjee, Rachna Banerjee, Jagadish Chandra Barma Basunia, Partha Bhowmick, Arup Chakraborty, Adhikari Deepak Dev, Sayani Ghosh, Bapi Haldar, Abu Teher Khan, Kalipada Saren Kherwal, Asit Kumar Mal, June Maliah, Mitali Bag, Kalilur Rahaman, Mala Roy, Sharmila Sarkar and Yusuf Pathan.In his petition, Abhishek Banerjee told the court on Tuesday that he had lodged the disqualification petition against the rebel MPs on June 18 and complained that despite the lapse of two months, no meaningful progress has been made on its adjudication.The continuing delay in the adjudication process is impacting democratic governance, he said.In the recently concluded Monsoon session, Banerjee had met the Speaker on Aug 12 to reiterate his demand for a speedy decision on the disqualification petitions submitted to him in June. Banerjee had earlier met Birla on July 27 in Parliament urging him to expedite his decision on the pending petitions.

Article Title: Beyond Ayodhya and the fish row: Why Nishad vote matters in Uttar Pradesh 2027 battle
Article Text:
The Nishad community finds itself at the centre of the fish row in Ayodhya ahead of 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly polls.

The 'fish on your plate' row

Sanjay Nishad said fish preparation mattered.

Ajay Rai dared CM Yogi Adityanath to provide evidence.

Nishads — the 'jal kisans'

2019 and 2022: Alliance and the unfinished bargain

SP and Congress try to prise open BJP's base

The VIP factor

The 2027 question

At a time when many Hindu devotees traditionally give up non-vegetarian food during 'Sawan', fish has acquired an unlikely political importance in Uttar Pradesh.The row began earlier this month with Uttar Pradesh minister and Nishad Party chief Sanjay Nishad's remark that fish cooked without garlic and onion could be considered vegetarian. It escalated on August 23, when a video purportedly showing fish being prepared at a Nishad community event in Ayodhya, attended by UP Congress president Ajay Rai, surfaced on social media.But behind the sparring over what was - or was not - on Rai's plate lies a larger electoral calculation. The Nishad vote has shifted political loyalties before, and with the BJP seeking to retain its non-Yadav OBC coalition and the opposition trying to prise open that support, the community could once again become an important factor in the 2027 contest.The controversy began earlier this month when Sanjay Nishad said at a programme: "Bina lahsun-pyaz ki bani machhli shakahari hai."The remark came during Sawan, a month when many Hindu devotees observe dietary restrictions, and quickly attracted attention because of the community he represents. Nishads have historically depended on rivers and water bodies for fishing, fish-rearing, boating and related livelihoods, making food and fishing practices part of a broader social and economic identity.Then came Ayodhya.On August 23, UP Congress president Ajay Rai travelled to Tarun, around 30 km from Ayodhya, after visiting Hanumangarhi, reciting the Hanuman Chalisa and offering prayers at the Ram temple. He attended a programme organised by members of the Nishad community. A video showing fish being prepared at the venue subsequently surfaced.The timing and location gave the BJP an opening.BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary described the alleged fish feast as "highly condemnable and unforgivable", while Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath accused Rai of "duplicity" for visiting a temple and then attending a fish feast during Sawan."You saw the conduct of the Congress state president yesterday. He goes to Hanumangarhi for darshan and, after coming out, enjoys a fish feast and then shouts 'Ram-Ram'," Adityanath said.Rai denied eating fish and challenged the CM to produce evidence. "If he can produce any pictures, I will be ready to resign immediately," he said.Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera defended the hosts, saying they belonged to the Nishad community and had their own traditions of eating and drinking.Later, cabinet minister Om Prakash Rajbhar entered the controversy, backing Nishad's earlier claim and asking Congress to clarify whether the fish allegedly served at the event had been cooked with garlic and onion."Sanjay Nishad machhli ke mahir hain, unhe zyada jaankari hai, hum thode kam hain," Rajbhar said.The political argument, however, goes well beyond the menu at one event. The larger story is the political importance of the community that hosted it.The Nishads are a cluster of riverine communities whose traditional livelihoods have been closely tied to rivers, ponds and other water bodies. Community organisations have increasingly used the term 'jal kisan', or water farmers, to describe this relationship.Fishing, fish-rearing, boating and the sale of fish have historically been central to these communities' economic lives. Questions over access to water bodies, fishing rights, sand mining and regulation of traditional occupations therefore have a direct political resonance.The term Nishad is also used as an umbrella for several communities and sub-castes, including Mallah, Kewat, Bind, Kashyap, Dhimar, Batham, Kahar, Manjhi and Turaha. Not all of these communities necessarily identify themselves as Nishad in the same way.In Uttar Pradesh, Nishads are classified among the Other Backward Classes (OBCs).Political estimates put the core Nishad population at around 4.5-5 per cent of the state's electorate. Estimates that include a wider set of related riverine communities put their combined share considerably higher.There is no recent official caste census providing a definitive figure, but the community's electoral importance comes less from its statewide percentage than from its concentration.Nishad voters have a significant presence across the Ganga-Yamuna belt and eastern Uttar Pradesh, including Gorakhpur, Varanasi, Azamgarh, Ballia, Mau, Ghazipur, Mirzapur, Bhadohi, Jaunpur and Prayagraj, besides parts of Sultanpur and Fatehpur.The community is considered electorally influential in more than 160 Assembly constituencies, with around 80 seats often identified as having a particularly substantial Nishad presence.That geographical concentration explains why a community accounting for a relatively small share of the state's electorate can command such political attention.The Nishad political identity is also deeply connected to stories from the Hindu epics.In the Ramayana, Nishadraj Guha, the boatman-king, is described as an ally of Ram during his exile. Guha receives Ram, Sita and Lakshman and helps them cross the Ganga.For the Nishad community, the story has long been invoked as a marker of their place within the Ram narrative — not as an identity created by contemporary politics, but as an older cultural association that acquired renewed political meaning during the Ram Janmabhoomi movement.The community also invokes Ekalavya from the Mahabharata, who is traditionally identified as belonging to the Nishad community. His story - of a skilled archer seeking to learn from Dronacharya and ultimately giving his thumb as guru dakshina - has come to represent a different strand of Nishad memory: talent, exclusion and the struggle for recognition.The two figures capture contrasting elements of the community's epic imagination: Nishadraj represents proximity to and loyalty towards Ram, while Ekalavya represents ability denied recognition.These narratives have subsequently been woven into the community's assertion of a distinct historical and social identity.Sections of the community found their cultural resonance in the Ram Janmabhoomi movement.As the campaign for a Ram temple in Ayodhya gathered momentum in the late 1980s and early 1990s, Nishad organisations and leaders participated in the wider mobilisation. The story of Nishadraj Guha gave the movement an immediate cultural connection for sections of the community, while the broader call for 'Ram Rajya' resonated with those who saw the temple campaign as a civilisational and cultural cause.The political landscape changed sharply after BJP leader LK Advani's Ram Rath Yatra in 1990, which transformed the temple issue into a mass political movement. The demolition of the Babri Masjid on December 6, 1992, further entrenched Ayodhya as a defining issue in BJP politics.As the BJP expanded its support among non-Yadav OBC communities, sections of the Nishad community also moved towards the party.But that support did not become a permanent political contract.Among sections of Nishad political opinion, a recurring grievance emerged: the community had supported the Ram movement but did not receive a commensurate political return.The complaint has, at various points, extended to BJP leaders associated with the Ram movement, including Advani and former UP CM Kalyan Singh, with Nishad voices arguing that their support for the Ram cause did not translate into adequate representation or resolution of longstanding demands regarding representation and farming on the riverside.In the coming years, the same community that participated in the Ram movement subsequently moved towards the Samajwadi Party, created its own political organisation and entered into an alliance with the BJP.That fluidity became particularly visible in the 1990s.Before the emergence of the Nishad Party, the strongest political association for sections of the community came through the social-justice politics of the Samajwadi Party.Phoolan Devi became the most recognisable symbol of that phase.A Mallah woman from Uttar Pradesh, Phoolan Devi contested the Mirzapur Lok Sabha seat on an SP ticket in 1996 and won. She retained the seat in 1999.Her rise gave the community an unusually prominent political figure and turned caste identity into a language of representation.Her political legacy continues to be invoked in Uttar Pradesh.The next major shift came in 2016, when Sanjay Nishad founded the Nirbal Indian Shoshit Hamara Aam Dal, popularly known as the Nishad Party.The party sought to consolidate riverine communities and give political expression to demands involving reservation, representation, fishing rights and livelihoods.Its first major electoral breakthrough came in an unlikely place.In the March 2018 Gorakhpur Lok Sabha bypoll, Praveen Nishad, Sanjay Nishad's son, contested as an SP-backed candidate and defeated the BJP.The result was politically significant because Gorakhpur had been Yogi Adityanath's parliamentary stronghold for five consecutive terms.The defeat demonstrated that the BJP's support among non-Yadav OBC communities could be disrupted when Nishad mobilisation combined with the SP's wider social coalition.But the equation soon changed again.Before the 2019 Lok Sabha election, the Nishad Party moved into the BJP-led NDA. Praveen Nishad joined the BJP and contested the Sant Kabir Nagar Lok Sabha seat on a BJP ticket, winning the election.The BJP-Nishad Party alliance became an important part of the BJP's strategy to consolidate non-Yadav OBC support in eastern Uttar Pradesh.The BJP and Nishad Party continued their alliance into the 2022 Uttar Pradesh assembly election.The BJP won 255 seats, while the Nishad Party won six. The NDA retained power with 273 seats in the 403-member assembly.For the BJP, the alliance helped reinforce its eastern Uttar Pradesh coalition.For Sanjay Nishad, however, being part of the government brought a different problem: once an ally enters government, its demands are increasingly judged against what it can actually secure from that government.The biggest unresolved issue remained the demand for Scheduled Caste status for sections of the Nishad community.Sanjay Nishad has repeatedly pressed the BJP government on the demand.On August 18, 2026, just months before the 2027 elections, he escalated the issue again, saying he was prepared to give up his ministerial position if necessary.His friction with the BJP had also become visible after the 2024 Lok Sabha election, when he blamed BJP leaders for his son Praveen Nishad's defeat in Sant Kabir Nagar.Praveen, who contested the seat on a BJP ticket, lost to the Samajwadi Party's Laxmikant Pappu Nishad.The result was another reminder that a BJP-Nishad Party alliance does not necessarily translate into a uniform Nishad vote.That fluidity is what the opposition is trying to exploit ahead of 2027.In March 2026, it appointed Sadhvi Niranjan Jyoti as chairperson of the Uttar Pradesh Backward Classes Commission. The move came alongside the BJP's continuing alliance with the Nishad Party.The SP responded by appointing Phoolan Devi's sister, 67-year-old Rukmini Devi, as president of the party's Uttar Pradesh women's wing. The appointment was seen as part of Akhilesh Yadav's PDA — Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak — outreach ahead of the 2027 election.Rukmini Devi subsequently attacked Sanjay Nishad, questioning what he had delivered for the community while being part of the government.The appointments show that the competition for the Nishad vote is not merely about alliances. It is a contest over who represents the community's political memory.Congress, on the other hand, has a more difficult task because its organisational presence among Nishads is weaker.Its August outreach in Tarun was therefore significant. Ajay Rai's visit to the Nishad community programme was an attempt to establish a direct connection with the community.The party's subsequent defence of the event, that the hosts were Nishads with their own food traditions, also allowed Congress to frame the controversy around community identity and traditional livelihoods rather than solely religious conduct.For the SP and Congress, the broader argument is that the Nishad vote is not synonymous with the Nishad Party.The Vikassheel Insaan Party (VIP), led by Bihar-based Nishad leader Mukesh Sahani, adds another layer to this contest.VIP entered Uttar Pradesh politics in the 2022 assembly election, seeking support among Nishads and other Extremely Backward Classes, particularly in Purvanchal.The party did not emerge as a major electoral force, but its campaign showed how smaller caste-based parties can complicate a close contest.VIP contested more than 100 seats, primarily in eastern Uttar Pradesh, and said its candidates polled more votes than Congress candidates in 15 constituencies, including Bairia, Bansdih, Phephna, Alapur, Jalalpur, Ghanghata, Balha, Shahganj and Kerakat.Its relationship with the BJP has been politically fluid rather than a straightforward alliance in Uttar Pradesh.Sahani has been a vocal critic of the BJP at various points. However, in neighbouring Bihar where the Nishads remain relevant across the seats in the Ganga area, his political trajectory has repeatedly shifted. VIP contested as part of the opposition Mahagathbandhan in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, switched to the NDA for the 2020 Bihar assembly election (winning 4 seats and entering the cabinet), but was dropped from the NDA in 2022 after contesting against the BJP in UP. In last year's Bihar polls, his party failed to secure any seat.However, in upcoming polls in UP, a few thousand votes in its favour can alter the results in close constituencies.The fish controversy may fade, but the political question it has exposed is unlikely to disappear.The BJP has the advantage of a long association with the Ram movement, an established organisational network and an alliance with the Nishad Party.The SP is seeking to revive the community's social-justice connection through Phoolan Devi's political legacy and the PDA framework.Congress is attempting to build a direct relationship with Nishad voters, while smaller parties such as VIP can potentially fragment the vote.For the Nishads themselves, however, the choice is unlikely to be framed around a single issue.Their political history has moved from the epic memory of Nishadraj and Ekalavya, to participation in the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, to the social-justice politics associated with Phoolan Devi, to the rise of the Nishad Party, its alliance with the BJP and subsequent friction over representation and reservation.The lesson from that history is clear: the Nishad vote has never been permanently owned by one party.In 2027, the contest will be over whether Ram and the BJP's organisational alliance can outweigh demands for reservation, representation and livelihoods - and whether the opposition can convert those demands into votes.
Article Summary: The nishad community finds itself at the centre of the fish row in ayodhya ahead of 2027 uttar pradesh assembly polls. Ajay rai dared cm yogi adityanath to provide evidence. Organiser of the event defended the decision to keep fish in the menu.

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday launched the 'Lokmata Ahilyabai Matrushakti Yatra' scheme and flagged off special buses to provide free travel facilities to women aged 60 years and above in the state.Speaking at the launch event in Lucknow, CM Yogi said the scheme was aimed at making the journey of women more convenient and dignified and strengthening their self-reliance."The maternal power that has eased the path of family and society throughout her life--our resolve to make her journey smooth and dignified is being realised in the double-engine government," the Chief Minister said.Under the scheme, women aged 60 years and above will be provided free bus travel facilities. The Chief Minister also said that on Raksha Bandhan, mothers, sisters and daughters would be provided free bus travel along with one accompanying person."The honour of maternal power and their convenience is our priority," CM Yogi said.The Chief Minister said the scheme has been named after Lokmata Ahilyabai Holkar, whom he described as an exemplary figure of women's self-reliance and good governance."At a time when the country was in the grip of the chaos caused by Mughal invaders, Lokmata Ahilyabai not only achieved the goals of good governance and preserved India's spiritual and cultural heritage but also set an exemplary standard for women's self-reliance," he said.CM Yogi said Ahilyabai Holkar had undertaken the restoration of several temples across the country that had been demolished or damaged by foreign invaders."Whenever the topic of women's self-reliance arises, we all recall the name of Lokmata Ahilyabai with deep reverence and respect," he said.The Chief Minister also launched a sharp attack on the previous governments in the state, alleging that women faced insecurity and lack of dignity before 2017."There was a time before 2017 when a particular slogan echoed among daughters, sisters, and mothers: '" CM Yogi said, referring to the Samajwadi Party.He alleged that the period was marked by concerns over women's safety and a lack of dedicated mechanisms such as integrated helplines, women's beat systems and women's help desks."There was no respect for them, let alone self-reliance; there were no integrated helplines, no women's beat systems, and no women's help desks," he said.CM Yogi further alleged that middlemen controlled pensions and scholarships and that mafia groups exercised influence over sectors including forest, sand, cattle and examination systems."Forest, sand, cattle, and exam-cheating mafias defined the state's identity; a mafia syndicate wielded power parallel to the actual government," he said.The Chief Minister said his government had, for the first time since Independence, formulated a comprehensive action plan aimed at integrating women, who constitute half of society, into governance schemes."This plan encompasses everything from a daughter's birth to her education, employment, and entrepreneurship, while also guaranteeing her safety and dignity; indeed, every scheme, decision, and budget of our government is dedicated to fulfilling these very objectives," he said.The Chief Minister had earlier announced the launch of the scheme in a post on X, saying the initiative was aimed at ensuring convenience and dignity for women."The maternal power that has eased the path of family and society throughout her life--our resolve to make her journey smooth and dignified is being realised in the double-engine government. Today in Lucknow, the 'Lokmata Ahilyabai Matrushakti Yatra' will be inaugurated, under which mothers and sisters of the state aged 60 years and above will be provided with free bus travel facilities," the post read."Additionally, on Raksha Bandhan, mothers, sisters, and daughters will be provided with free bus travel facilities, including one accompanying traveller. The honour of maternal power and their convenience is our priority," he added.The scheme comes as the Uttar Pradesh government seeks to expand measures focused on women's welfare, mobility and self-reliance.

Article Title: Who are India's NEET youth? What NITI's 8.7 crore figure really tells us
Article Text:
AI generated representational image

Reimagining Skilling for Viksit Bharat@2047

What exactly is NEET?

Unpacking what is NEET

The Covid factor

NEET youth have an information problem

The money problem

Courses have 'weak outcome orientation'

Reasons behind feeling disconnected

An illustrative pathway

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Development as Freedom

During election coverage, a common refrain among older folks is their concern that young people are sitting at home without jobs, sometimes not even looking for one, happily scrolling through reels. Talk to young people and they often speak of a lack of coherent job opportunities or the skills that match the demands of the market.These often-heard anecdotes are given a more coherent shape in, a new report from the government's policy think tank NITI Aayog . The report attempts a candid diagnosis of where India is, and how it can become a developed nation by 2047, the centenary of Independence.Beyond merely ticking boxes on broad numbers of people trained, the report examines the barriers that determine whether skilling actually leads to work. Money, information, mobility, family circumstances, access to institutions and exposure to the workplace all matter. In that sense, it also tells a larger story about how the circumstances into which a young person is born can influence where he or she gets slotted in life.The report focuses, among others, on a group of young Indians who do not fit neatly into the conventional categories. They are neither in school or college, nor employed or undergoing training. Policy researchers have an acronym for them: NEET, or Not in Education, Employment or Training.NITI Aayog's new report puts 8.7 crore people in a NEET youth bucket in its map of India's population. After the figure was interpreted in some reports as a measure of unemployment, the government issued a clarification. It said the 8.7 crore estimate refers to young people who were not seeking employment, while the unemployed form a separate category drawn from a different population base.In the NITI report, NEET youth are defined as those aged 15 to 29 who are not engaged in education, employment or training. The footnote describes approximately nine crore as "NEET excluding seeking jobs", based on the NSS 78th Round of 2021, and says roughly 88% were engaged in domestic duties.In its clarification, the government has provided further clarity. It said the category includes young people engaged in voluntary work or household enterprises, attending to domestic duties, unable to work because of a health condition, spending leisure time, and others.NITI's population exhibit starts with an estimated 145 crore Indians. It shows 65.4 crore, or 45.1%, in the labour force, and 79.6 crore, or 54.9%, outside it.Among those in the labour force, the exhibit shows 29.23 crore in agriculture, 34.24 crore in non-agricultural work and around 2 crore unemployed. The unemployed are part of the labour force because they are seeking employment.The population outside the labour force is split into roughly 29.1 crore students, 11.3 crore children below five, 15.7 crore people aged 59-plus, 14.7 crore in other categories and 8.7 crore NEET youth.There is another important qualification. The 8.7 crore estimate is based on the NSS 78th Round of 2021, which included a Multiple Indicator Survey (MIS) to assess different socio-economic parameters. The government subsequently pointed out that the data used to calculate this figure was collected in FY2020-21, during the Covid-19 pandemic, when education and employment were severely disrupted. It said the figure could therefore represent a deviation from the normal trajectory.The government points to the latest PLFS to say that the youth NEET percentage is now "significantly lower". The PLFS Annual Report 2025 estimates that 25.0% of Indians aged 15 to 29 were not in employment, education or training under the usual-status measure. For those aged 15 to 24, the corresponding figure was 21.0%.The NITI report itself warns that its population exhibit is a "static snapshot" constructed using different datasets, including PLFS, UDISE, AISHE and NSS, with reference years ranging from 2021 to 2024.NITI followed a mixed-method approach across five groups of school students, tertiary learners, formal and informal non-agricultural workers, NEET youth, and women as a cross-cutting segment. Agriculture was excluded because NITI says the sector requires a separate analytical framework.Its quantitative evidence draws on the MSDE State of Skills Survey 2024, covering roughly 8,000 learners, and BCG's Higher Education Survey 2023, covering roughly 4,000, supplemented by more than 60 in-depth interviews, focus groups and industry conversations.Among surveyed NEET youth who had not undertaken or completed a skilling programme, 43% cited lack of awareness of the right programmes as one of their top three reasons for not pursuing skilling. The corresponding proportion was 55% among informal workers, 52% among formal workers, 47% among women and 36% among higher-education students.The report says young people often make choices based on examination scores, family preferences, cost or social prestige rather than a clear understanding of what exactly is needed to get a job. Vocational education and ITIs are often viewed as second-tier options, while online courses are often perceived as unreliable.NITI describes affordability as a "binding constraint".NEET youth, it says, face the particular disadvantage of having no income while also carrying the sunk cost of their previous education. In simple terms, that is the cost already incurred on an education that may not have translated into work.For low-income workers, even a free course can be expensive if attending it means losing wages. In other words, the opportunity cost of training can remain high even when the course itself is free.The report shows how price-sensitive the wider skilling market is. More than 80% of informal workers who undertake skilling do so either free or for less than ₹10,000. Among women who undergo skilling, 72% either take a free course or pay less than ₹5,000, compared with 52% of men.NITI's prescription for NEET youth is based on understanding this ground reality. It advocates affordable or subsidised training with financial support, along with the ability to combine learning with earning instead of having to stop work for weeks or months.NITI says 82% of NEET respondents report a foundational gap in existing skilling programmes involving job-interview preparation and placement tie-ups.This is where the report turns its gaze on the skilling system itself. NITI describes "weak outcome orientation" as a "core limitation" of many existing skilling programmes. It says programmes often prioritise enrolment and completion over placement, progression or income outcomes.That observation becomes significant when set against the sheer scale of India's skilling push. The report says more than 7.67 crore individuals have been trained since 2014-15, while around ₹34,000 crore was allocated towards skilling-related expenditure across central ministries in FY2025-26.The government, meanwhile, says it has begun implementing some of the report's recommendations. It points to the ₹600 crore Integrated Scheme in Skilling Architecture (ISSA) announced in the Union Budget 2026-27 as part of an effort to strengthen convergence across education, skilling, employment and lifelong learning.The problem NITI identifies is visible even among people still in education.It says 80% of higher-education students cite lack of practical experience and industry exposure as a major pain point, while 47% of formal workers identify lack of prior work experience and internships as the top challenge when finding new jobs.Among undergraduate students dissatisfied with their education outcome, 34% cited lacking skills and 18% inadequate interview preparation. Among higher-education students aspiring to entrepreneurship, the report says 61% are unaware of pathways to pursue it.The larger point is that a degree by itself does not guarantee workplace readiness. Somewhere between the classroom, the training centre and the employer, the route from learning to earning needs to be more robust.NITI uses a character called "Meera" to illustrate how its proposed system might work.In the illustration, she gains some vocational exposure in school but drops out following household constraints and early marriage at 18, becoming NEET. She then discovers a nearby short-term beauty course, receives a skill voucher, moves into a nearby part-time salon job and ultimately towards self-employment.In NITI's illustration, that part-time job pays ₹15,000 a month, before she starts taking clients independently.The point is that for someone who has dropped out of both learning and earning, the route back is unlikely to be a single jump from NEET to a permanent salaried job. It will generally go through a short course, flexible work and then a steadier livelihood.The official unemployment count, then, is only one measure. What also matters is whether young Indians stay connected to at least one of three systems of education, training or earning.NITI's findings point to something larger than a skills gap. They also point to a privilege gap.Bridging that privilege gap may be the most sober takeaway from NITI's roadmap to 2047. India's demographic dividend will not be realised merely by counting how many people receive training certificates. It will depend on whether young Indians, irrespective of the circumstances they start with, have a credible route from learning to earning.As economist and philosopher Amartya Sen wrote in, "Development can be seen … as a process of expanding the real freedoms that people enjoy."
Article Summary: Niti aayog report attempts a candid diagnosis of where india is, and how it can become a developed nation by 2047. Money, information, mobility, family circumstances, access to institutions and exposure to the workplace all matter.

Article Title: Over 76 lakh women registered under Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna: Punjab CM Mann

Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann on Wednesday said 76.11 lakh women have been registered under the state government's Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna.He said a sum of Rs 2,381 crore has already been transferred into the accounts of 68.06 lakh women.Under the Mukh Mantri Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojana, women from the general category receive Rs 1,000 per month, while those belonging to the Scheduled Castes get Rs 1,500.Mann said the Punjab government's commitment to women's welfare would remain unwavering and the financial aid scheme for women would not be discontinued as long as the AAP remained in power in Punjab.He also said a sum of Rs 52.20 crore has been transferred to the accounts of 1.37 lakh 'Satkar Sakhis', while recognising their contribution in taking this scheme to women across Punjab.The chief minister said 'Satkar Sakhis' would receive Rs 300 for every registration, enabling them to earn more than Rs 200 crore through the initiative."'Satkar Sakhis' have played a crucial role in taking this scheme to women across Punjab. Their dedicated efforts have enabled more than 75 lakh women to get registered under the Mukh Mantri Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna," he said.Addressing a gathering virtually, Mann said his government launched the scheme in recognition of the dignity and respect of women.This financial assistance may not make women rich, but it will certainly provide them dignity and self-respect. Women deserve the highest respect because they are the source of life itself, and the blessings of mothers and sisters can help overcome every challenge in the world, he stated.Punjab AAP's women wing president and MLA Amandeep Kaur also lauded the dedicated contribution of 'Satkar Sakhis' and the entire women wing in taking the Mukh Mantri Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna to women across Punjab, saying they were not merely helping women fill forms but were becoming a source of support in transforming their lives.PTI

Article Title: Over 61,000 wait for kidney transplants
Article Text:
India performed 11,558 livingdonor and 1,918 deceased-donor kidney transplants in 2024, while 61,668 patients remained on the waiting list as of Feb 9.

NEW DELHI: India faces a widening gap between demand for kidney transplants and the availability of donor organs, with 61,668 patients on the waiting list, nearly five times the number of kidney transplants performed as of Feb 9, a parliamentary standing committee has said.The committee on health and family welfare has recommended that kidney transplant facilities be expanded to at least three govt medical colleges in large states and one in every small state and UT, besides setting time-bound targets to increase organ retrieval centres and transplant infrastructure, particularly in underserved and hilly regions.India performed 11,558 living-donor and 1,918 deceased-donor kidney transplants in 2024, while 61,668 patients remained on the waiting list as of Feb 9. The committee — in its report tabled in the recently concluded monsoon session of Parliament — said the figures highlight the widening mismatch between demand and capacity and the continued dependence on living donors.It said transplant activity remains concentrated in a handful of states and metropolitan centres, including Delhi, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Karnataka, leaving access uneven across the country.The committee attributed the shortage partly to India’s low deceased-organ donation rates, citing social misconceptions, inadequate awareness, limited organ retrieval infrastructure and procedural bottlenecks. It has called for a nationwide behavioural-change campaign and stronger hospital-based organ retrieval and transplant coordination systems.Data from the National Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisation for 2019-23 showed that women constituted 63.8% of living organ donors, while men accounted for 69.8% of transplant recipients. The committee has sought a study to determine whether socioeconomic, cultural, financial or gender-related barriers contribute to the disparity.
Article Summary: India performed 11,558 livingdonor and 1,918 deceased-donor kidney transplants in 2024. 61,668 patients remained on the waiting list as of feb 9. Committee on health and family welfare has recommended that kidney transplant facilities be expanded to at least three govt medical colleges.

Article Title: 6 dead, 3 hurt as vehicle falls into gorge in J&K’s Poonch
Article Text:
All victims and injured were residents of Seri Chouhana, police said.

JAMMU: Six people died and three others, including an 11-year-old boy, were injured after the vehicle they were travelling in skidded off the road and plunged into a deep gorge in Surankote in J&K’s Poonch district on Wednesday.The accident occurred around 5.30pm. Officials suspected the driver had lost control of the vehicle, which rolled into the gorge, killing six occupants — Mohd Shafiq (32), Nazakat Hussain (34), Sheraz Ahmed (30), Musarat Naz (19), Mohd Fareed (21), and Zulfat Bi (25) — on the spot, police said.Upon receiving information, cops reached the spot and launched a rescue operation with the help of locals. Poonch chief medical officer Dr Parvaiz Ahmed Khan pressed ambulances into service to facilitate evacuation. The injured were initially admitted to a local health facility, from where two were shifted to GMC Jammu due to their critical condition, Dr Khan said.All victims and injured were residents of Seri Chouhana, police said, adding that the bodies were shifted to Poonch district hospital.J&K Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha condoled the tragedy in an X post, stating that he had directed the district administration to provide immediate assistance to the affected families. Poonch deputy commissioner Ashok Kumar Sharma and other senior civil administrative officials visited the hospital.

JAMMU: Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) busted a major cross-border heroin trafficking cartel in Jammu, seizing 5.2 kg of heroin, and arresting the suspected mastermind and two of his accomplices.“On a tip-off on Aug 22, a vehicle was intercepted in Jammu‘s Panjtirthi and two of its occupants, both residents of Kashmir’s Baramulla district, were arrested for possessing the contraband,” an NCB spokesperson said Wednesday.“Preliminary investigation led NCB to another resident of Baramulla, the suspected mastermind. He was traced and arrested in Leh on Aug 24. The seized drug, suspected to have been smuggled from Pakistan, entered India through the Uri border sector,” the NCB official said.“The probe will identify cross-border suppliers, financial links, transporters, local associates, and the intended distribution network,” the spokesperson added.The operation follows two other heroin seizures on Aug 12 and on Aug 13.NCB has urged citizens to actively support the fight against drug trafficking and contribute towards the objective of a ‘Nasha Mukt’ Bharat.
